# Network sub-actions

## HTTP request

Visits a web address and saves the answer. Use it to call other websites or tools, like fetching a joke or poking a smart device.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **Method** | GET asks for information. POST sends information. PUT, PATCH and DELETE change or remove things on the other side. HEAD asks only for the headline details. Options: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD. Starts as: `GET`. |
| **URL** | The full web address, starting with http:// or https://, like "https://example.com/api". |
| **Headers** | Extra details sent along, one per line as "Name: value". Most people can leave this empty. |
| **Body** | The data to send with a POST, PUT or PATCH. Leave empty if you send nothing. |
| **Content type** | What kind of data the body is. application/json is right for JSON. Only used when there is a body. Starts as: `application/json`. |
| **Timeout (seconds)** | How many seconds to wait for an answer before giving up. The most is 30. Starts as: `30`. |
| **Store response in argument** | The name of the variable that will hold the answer. Use it later as %httpResponse% (or the name you type). Starts as: `httpResponse`. |
| **Parse result as JSON** | Tick if the answer is JSON data. Each value in it also gets its own variable, like %httpResponse.name%. Starts as: `false`. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%httpResponse%` | The answer text (or the name you chose in the box above) |
| `%httpStatusCode%` | The result number: 200 means it worked, 404 means not found |
| `%httpSuccess%` | True if the request worked |
| `%httpHeaders%` | The extra details that came back |
| `%httpError%` | What went wrong, if the request failed or timed out |

<small>Type id: `core.httpRequest`</small>

## UDP broadcast

Sends a short text message to other devices on your network, or to this computer, with no reply expected. Handy for small gadgets or other apps that listen.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **UDP port** | The door number the other app listens on, from 1 to 65535. Check that app's settings. Starts as: `6669`. |
| **Payload** | The text to send. |
| **Address** | Who to send it to. 255.255.255.255 shouts to every device on your home network. 127.0.0.1 means this computer. You can also type one device's address. Starts as: `255.255.255.255`. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%udpBytesSent%` | How many bytes were sent |

<small>Type id: `core.udpBroadcast`</small>
